chain.label: VFR flight confined to narrow low-altitude East River exclusion corridor
chain.trigger: the accident airplane's altitude varied from 500 to 700 feet for the remainder of the flight ... it approached the northern end of the East River exclusion where the floor of the class B airspace transitioned from 1,100 feet to the surface, effectively requiring either a 180 degree turn to reverse course or an ATC clearance

chain.label: 13-knot easterly wind causing westward drift and reduced effective turn width
chain.trigger: the 13-knot easterly wind caused a measurable westward drift ... the effective turn width available was reduced to about 1,400 feet

chain.label: Neither pilot had flown the East River exclusion; owner low-time and not recent
chain.trigger: there was no record that he had previously flown in the New York East River class B exclusion airspace ... In the last 90 days, 30 days, and 24 hours before the accident flight, he flew 13.7, 0, and 0 hours

chain.label: Inadequate planning: flew north up the East River without allowing for limited turning space or requesting class B clearance
chain.trigger: The pilots should have recognized, during preflight planning or while they were considering flying up the East River ... that there was limited turning space in the East River exclusion area ... Alternatively, the pilots could have chosen to contact ATC and request clearance

caused_by.evidence: requiring either a 180 degree turn to reverse course or an ATC clearance to enter the class B airspace
no record that he had previously flown in the New York East River class B exclusion airspace

chain.label: 180-degree downwind turn begun from mid-channel at only 40-45 degrees bank instead of the required 50 degrees
chain.trigger: the actual turn was accomplished with a bank angle of 40 degrees to 45 degrees ... The pilots did not aggressively bank the airplane throughout the turn nor did they use the full available width of the river

caused_by.evidence: The pilots should have recognized ... that they would need to maximize the lateral distance available for turning

By starting the turn on the west side of the river and turning into the wind, a minimum bank angle of 35 degrees would have been needed, rather than the minimum 50 degrees required by turning in the direction of the wind

chain.label: Turn still incomplete as airplane closed on the western shoreline and Manhattan buildings
chain.trigger: The airplane was only about 75 percent through the 180 degree turn when it approached the western shoreline of the East River

caused_by.evidence: Because the turn was initiated at 40 degrees to 45 degrees rather than the minimally required 50 degrees
the 13-knot easterly wind caused a measurable westward drift

chain.label: Bank steepened past the stall boundary while pulling through the turn; aerodynamic stall
chain.trigger: it is likely that the pilots put the airplane into an aerodynamic stall while pulling through the turn ... If the bank angle exceeded 61 degrees, the airplane wing would aerodynamically stall

caused_by.evidence: the pilots increased the bank angle of the airplane to attempt completion of the 180 degree turn
a sufficiently greater bank angle would have been required as the turn progressed, which would have placed the airplane dangerously close to an aerodynamic stall at relatively low altitude

chain.label: Uncontrolled descent from about 600 feet with no altitude for recovery
chain.trigger: the wings were 'wobbling,' like the pilot was fighting for control. The airplane then pitched down and to the right and descended ... this is the approximate location where the airplane began to descend

caused_by.evidence: it is likely that the pilots put the airplane into an aerodynamic stall while pulling through the turn
the accident airplane was at an altitude of 600 feet before the 180 degree turn was initiated

chain.label: Impact with apartment building at 333 feet above street level and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted a 520-foot tall apartment building at 524 East 72nd Street, 333 feet above street level ... destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: The airplane then pitched down and to the right and descended below his field of view prior to impact
